title: Reduce complete relative-tariff replay time by 29.42% (no κ)
body:
## Summary

An exact integer Horner backend reduces the complete frozen PR6378 primary relative-tariff replay's median wall time by **29.42%**, from **49.18 ms to 34.71 ms**, while preserving both rational interval endpoints, the complete result bytes and every original CLI check.

```text
same frozen source + same complete CLI
original: per-term Fraction Taylor sum
integer:  integer Horner recurrence + identical rational tail
result:   identical 5805-byte retained certificate
```

Claim type: **scoped exact-arithmetic preservation proof and measured verifier-engineering improvement**, with finite corroboration. This contribution is produced by Nick Petalas. ToikY retains the scientific theorem, primary verifier and independent oracle; DreamingOfClouds, Ali Romman and the full retained NOTICE keep their construction/caller/native credit. Classical Horner and Taylor methods are not claimed as new.

Only `research/relative-tariff-integer-exp/` is added. Sixteen exact predecessor files are retained at PR6378 head `4cfe905d84f3720c23a7f155f615222401953f95`, including the original NOTICE. The adapter modifies one private function binding. No shared source or selected frontier changes.

## Evidence

- Before: nine alternating fresh-process samples have median **49.178584 ms**, range **48.438583 to 52.462125 ms**. After: median **34.710583 ms**, range **34.038625 to 36.006292 ms**. All eighteen measured commands and two warmups succeed. Both arms include the same adapter/source-authentication overhead and execute the original complete CLI, including the typed and byte-exact result comparison. Generated `BENCHMARK.json` binds twenty source/measurement inputs. This is one recorded host and command, not a universal or all-command speed claim.
- A separate profile identifies 72 exponential evaluations as the limiter, 25.4 ms of the 43.6 ms instrumented source run. Their 1728 per-term rational iterations become integer arithmetic. Profiling is excluded from the benchmark. Both arms retain the same degree, grids, source fixture and existing logarithm cache.
- The written proof preserves the finite Taylor polynomial and its exact geometric tail for every rational `0<=x<=1/4` and degree `n>=1`. The bounded implementation accepts Fraction components up to 4096 bits and degrees 1..64; the actual source uses degree 24 and denominators up to 171 bits.
- Local CPython 3.12.15/macOS arm64 normal and optimized replay pass: **1449** exact direct-power/factorial cases, every reached source argument, complete result equality, both complete CLIs, **14** negative controls and all **3** inherited scientific rejection controls. Each registered check takes about **0.30 seconds** locally.
- Registered package metadata/replay, syntax parsing, whitespace checks and exact committed-byte/source-history preflight pass at `968c7cbf16dc74459dbe836401f7469b61474b52`. All sixteen retained files match the generated origins manifest. No unmerged Git object or network access is required by the replay.

From the repository root, with the standard library:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/relative-tariff-integer-exp/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -O -B research/relative-tariff-integer-exp/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/relative-tariff-integer-exp
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/relative-tariff-integer-exp --check-source-history
```

Expected markers: `PASS_RELATIVE_TARIFF_INTEGER_EXP`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. Another CPython 3.12 executable can replace the local interpreter path. A fresh benchmark uses `benchmark.py --pairs 9 --output /tmp/relative-tariff-timings.json`, with the same interpreter flags and an unoccupied output path.

## Limitations

The predecessor tariff theorem is a cited premise, not an audit deliverable. This accelerates one complete primary command; predecessor profile producers and the independent tariff oracle are authenticated where the primary authenticates them but are not executed or accelerated here. No new root, kappa, native/caller/supplier admission, complete multiplication theorem or selected-frontier change is claimed. The five framework assumptions remain. No independent human or formal proof-kernel review is claimed. Lean, Docker, physical integration and the selected cold replay are unrun.

## Open next questions

- Does this exact kernel improve another actual source-bound caller? Start by profiling that complete command and binding its exact interval contract. No other caller is covered here.
- Should a future primary relative-tariff verifier adopt it? Bind that exact new source head and retain its complete receipt and rejection checks; shared adoption and changed-head applicability remain separate decisions.

## Related open work

Refreshed this account's fifteen open PRs created since the advance CLAIM. None adds work on the same frozen PR6378 primary relative-tariff command or computes a conflicting result for it.

- #6378 supplies the frozen complete primary relative-tariff command and scientific result used here. All interval endpoints and complete certificate bytes are preserved; its proof and independent oracle remain credited and unchanged.
- #6375 supplies the shared-carrier construction whose frozen profiles that command compares. This contribution changes no word, paid/productive invoice or claimed kappa.
- #6416 independently studies the same PR6375 scalar prefix and owned functionals. This runtime change supplies no additional endpoint or erasure evidence.
- #6372 supplies the predecessor construction used in the frozen OLD profile; its native/caller obligations are outside this performance claim.
- #6353 supplies an earlier construction in the retained profile lineage; this contribution changes none of its invoices or admission obligations.
- #6398 uses a changed mixed caller; this adapter supplies no admission evidence for that caller.
- #6399 changes the native construction; its invoice is outside this frozen replay fixture.
- #6401 composes the changed native and mixed caller; this adapter does not accelerate or validate its accounting proof.
- #6417 publishes the changed native/mixed-caller conditional proposal; its separate claim is unaffected here.

[Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19361553). Live claims, open/account PRs, local reservations and main/merged object and formula searches were checked before claiming and committing. Sparse local notes and unpublished work remain coverage limits.

## CI notes

Both `plan` and `replay (research/relative-tariff-integer-exp)` passed at commit `968c7cbf16dc74459dbe836401f7469b61474b52` in [run 41536234280](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41536234280). The registered normal and optimized conformance checks are now hosted-CI certified. Local metadata, direct replay, timings and committed-byte/source-history checks also passed.

Hosted replay checks exact conformance and source/timing-receipt bindings. It does not certify the local speed percentage as a cross-host threshold, the written proof through a formal kernel, or supplier admission.
